Continues the SAME approved Shelv portal rebuild: D01–D48, 26 approved screens, secondary flows and 10 required journeys. Draft PR; no merge or production deployment authorized.

Acceptance remains **1 bounded capability (own Account Name persistence), 0/26 complete screens, 0/10 complete journeys**. M01's actual Auth/browser/SQL/isolation/recovery/result-after-logout evidence has independent R2 PASS. Implementation counts remain 24/26 mounted and12/26 complete SOURCE wiring, separate from acceptance.

The genuine M02 Orders attempt found a fixture compatibility defect: ordinary OTP/PKCE200 and fixed RPC200 became client503 because the approved seed used a policy URL under forbidden .invalid. The production validator correctly refused it. Current359c changes only the fixture URL to example.com and adds a production-DTO fixture regression. Full Source R3 passes22/22 +32/32 +16 independent controls; this is not genuine corrected-case acceptance. All prior bad rows, original descriptors, failed browser traces and raw runs are unchanged. The failed3d case is STOPPED_RETAINED with all65 native commands0/joined and dump/evidence/containers/volume/network/keys retained; no post-stop query/reuse/reset. Actual baseline/final A/B complete observations and all27 protected relation digests match.

Current commit also admits the complete Source R4 notification assets closing NIR1/NIR2/NIR3. Their42/42 controls do not accept notifications; actual publication-generated IDs and genuine verification remain pending.

Validation: **204 affected Source/data controls pass in both Root and Portal cwd**, zero skips. Production runtime, shared URL validation, Auth/RLS and all68 migrations are unchanged. Exact-head hosted CI and Codex review are separate pending gates.

Next: a NEW uniquely owned valid-URL Orders case, then deliberate advisor publication feeding notification acknowledgement and immutable history. No real clients, money, purchases, fulfillment or external emails. Guidance private-return/M65/provider-photo/A07 holds remain HELD.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject invalid version routes before creating a history controller**

For an authenticated client opening `/history/versions/0` or `/history/versions/not-a-version`, `parseRoute` accepts the version as a generic identifier and `ClientHistoryContent` converts it to `0` or `NaN`. This effect then calls `createVersionController`, which synchronously throws `TypeError('invalid version')`. Because there is no application error boundary, the malformed deep link crashes the React application instead of showing the existing unavailable/recovery UI. Validate the positive safe-integer version before mounting `HistoricalPlan`, or handle the rejected value here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **GPT-6.1 Sol responding on behalf of KanujVerma**

Fixed in 9aac7eb143738c7789c7f39df9bb89031a61f00c, included in the current head 1a6a42b595086c6bc8f32553abda1dc321e3641e. ClientHistoryContent validates the positive safe-integer conversion before mounting HistoricalPlan or its restoration scope, and invalid tokens show shared recovery back to History. Route grammar and valid-version behavior are preserved.

Current SSR regressions pass8/8, selected retained History/navigation/restoration70/70, and independent additional recovery6/6. The original corrected SSR program gives3pass/5 missing-recovery assertion failures; the mounted-effect throw is source-deduced, not an observed SSR TypeError. Independent complete five-path review4531aae4 is scoped PASS. Mounted browser/genuine acceptance remains open.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use a Workers-supported redirect mode for private fetches**

In the actual Cloudflare Worker runtime, this fetch throws before sending any request because Workers does not support `redirect: 'error'`; [Cloudflare documents that it immediately raises a TypeError](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/request/#parameters). The catch converts that exception into a 503, so every notification inbox/read/write operation fails even with valid credentials and a healthy backend. The new photo-inventory fetch in `client-upstream.ts:69` has the same defect and makes photo inventory unavailable as well. Use `redirect: 'manual'` and explicitly reject 3xx responses, as the existing shared response helper and the integrated Account/Orders transports already do.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
